tasks.short: Check applications against the job requirements for each site and shift.

today.trigger: An application arrives in Recruitee or a manager changes an approved vacancy.
steps: Read the vacancy and confirm essential requirements with the hiring manager.
Read applications for relevant experience, qualifications, site preferences and shift availability.
Contact applicants where information is missing or unclear.
Record findings in Recruitee and prepare candidates for a selection decision.
drudgery: Reading the same information across CVs and application forms
Copying evidence into notes
Repeatedly checking whether a certificate is essential on entry or can be obtained during onboarding
today.time_sinks: Inconsistent CV formats, vague vacancy requirements and missing shift information create repeated reading and follow-up.

lenses.faster: Extract job-related evidence into a standard checklist with links to the original application. Repeated reading and copying largely disappear.
lenses.autonomous: A new application triggers extraction, completeness checks and a review task. Missing evidence remains unknown; the workflow does not reject applicants.
lenses.ambitious: Give every applicant a consistent evidence review, including people with unconventional CVs or experience gained through agency work.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive document checking and leave more time to understand transferable skills and discuss practical job requirements.
lenses.options: Show evidence against several suitable open roles across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, subject to the applicant's stated preferences.
lenses.altitude: Maintain the screening requirements, inspect extraction errors and improve questions that repeatedly produce incomplete answers.
reach: Help HR Business Partners clarify vacancy requirements.
Help Learning and Development distinguish entry requirements from skills that onboarding can teach.

tasks.human_edge: Recognising transferable experience, challenging unnecessary requirements and deciding whether missing evidence deserves a conversation.
tasks.pattern_why: An llm_step extracts evidence from unstructured applications; deterministic checks organise it. An agent_with_gate prepares the review, but a recruiter checks the sources before any selection consequence, so the earlier automate classification does not justify autonomous matching decisions.

in_practice.trigger: A new application event reaches a proposed workflow through Recruitee webhooks.
steps: Load the approved, versioned requirements for that vacancy and remove unnecessary personal fields from model input.
Extract relevant evidence with document references, marking missing or contradictory information explicitly.
Apply written completeness rules without producing an overall suitability score or automatic rejection.
Present every application to the recruiter with the evidence checklist and original documents.
Save recruiter corrections and the approved screening note in Recruitee; route technical failures to a manual queue.
in_practice.human_gate: The recruiter checks the underlying application and approves each screening conclusion before it can affect referral or rejection.
systems: Approved LLM service, subject to procurement
data_needed: Approved essential and trainable requirements by role, site and shift
Application documents and answers
Applicant-stated location and shift preferences
Evidence supplied for relevant qualifications
Approved screening examples and correction rules
in_practice.logs_to: Recruitee screening notes and a restricted integration log containing requirement version, source references, model version, corrections and reviewer; logs follow applicant retention rules.

evidence.claim: Recruitee documents webhooks that can support an event-triggered integration; the proposed evidence extraction is additional work.
Evidence extraction with source checks is plausible; 60% recruiter effort saved and 2 times faster task turnaround are unmeasured planning estimates.

risks: CV wording, career gaps or language fluency can become unfair proxies; do not infer protected characteristics or treat missing information as a failed requirement.
Applications can contain misleading text or instructions aimed at the model; treat all application content as untrusted data.

AI used to evaluate or filter applicants can fall within the EU AI Act's high-risk employment category even with human review. The Commission's current timeline places Annex III high-risk rules from 2 December 2027; classify the intended use and prepare the applicable controls. [European Commission AI Act guidance](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)
Assess AVG lawful basis, necessity, processor terms and whether a DPIA is required before processing live applications, including during a pilot.
research_questions: On a representative sample across sites and job families, how often does extraction miss evidence that a recruiter considers material?
Can managers agree on essential versus trainable requirements before applications arrive?
Does measured checking and correction time leave at least half the current screening effort saved?
Can the vendor and privacy adviser support the intended use, retention controls and AI Act classification?

tasks.short: Explain the job, shifts, pay and working conditions clearly to applicants.

today.trigger: An applicant asks a question, enters an interview stage or receives an offer.
steps: Check the vacancy, applicable CAO and current approved employment terms.
Confirm site-specific shifts, working conditions and training expectations with the manager.
Explain the details by phone, email or interview.
Record questions and resolve exceptions with the relevant HR specialist.
systems: AFAS Profit for authorised employment terms
drudgery: Rewriting the same explanations about shifts and allowances
Finding the current policy or salary information
Correcting inconsistent descriptions between vacancies and emails
today.time_sinks: Information is spread across job records, policies and manager knowledge; unusual pay or scheduling questions need several hand-offs.

lenses.faster: Assemble an approved job information pack from structured role, site, shift and employment-term fields. Recruiters stop rebuilding routine explanations.
lenses.autonomous: Send the relevant approved pack when an applicant reaches a specified stage. Route questions outside the approved answers to the recruiter.
lenses.ambitious: Give every warehouse, transport and office applicant a realistic preview before interview, including shifts, workplace conditions and week-one training.
lenses.joy: Keep the conversations about motivation and practical concerns while removing repeated policy recitation.
lenses.options: Prepare short, detailed and translated versions of the same approved information, with specialist review of pay terminology.
lenses.altitude: Own the clarity and accuracy of candidate information and use recurring questions to improve vacancy briefs.
reach: Prepare onboarding information with HR Administration.
Identify unclear employment-term explanations for Compensation and Benefits.

tasks.human_edge: Explaining difficult trade-offs, noticing hesitation and discussing individual circumstances without making promises beyond the approved offer.
tasks.pattern_why: Use deterministic_software to select approved information and populate templates. A copilot can draft clearer wording offline, but routine sending does not need a model to interpret CAOs or invent answers.

in_practice.trigger: An applicant reaches a configured information stage in Recruitee.
steps: Select the approved job pack using role, site, employment route, shift and applicable CAO.
Validate required fields and the effective date of pay and policy information.
Send the approved pack through Recruitee, including a named recruiter contact.
Assign unanswered questions and individual negotiations to the recruiter or relevant specialist.
Record recurring questions and send proposed wording changes to the content owner for approval.
in_practice.human_gate: Compensation and Benefits approves pay content; site managers approve working conditions. The recruiter handles exceptions and negotiations before any individual commitment.
data_needed: Versioned role and site information
Applicable CAO and approved pay and allowance tables
Shift patterns and contract hours
Training and certificate expectations
Approved benefits and progression explanations
in_practice.logs_to: Recruitee message history records the recipient, template version and job pack sent; SharePoint records content approval and effective dates.

evidence.claim: Recruitee workflow automations can send emails and create tasks following configured events; available functionality depends on the subscription.
A versioned information library could remove much routine explanation; 50% effort saved and 1.5 times faster turnaround remain estimates.

risks: Selecting the wrong CAO, contract route or shift can produce misleading pay information; stop sending when required fields or approvals are missing.
Translations can change the meaning of allowances, guaranteed hours or progression; review these passages before use.
Applicants may not read email or may need a conversation; offer an accessible human contact and record unresolved questions.

Any later interactive AI assistant would need its own accuracy controls and clear disclosure that it is AI. [European Commission enforcement guidance](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/enforcement-ai-act)
research_questions: What share of applicant questions can be answered entirely from approved content?
Who can keep CAO, allowance and site information current, and how quickly can expired content be blocked?
Do realistic job previews improve offer acceptance and 90-day retention without increasing misunderstanding?
Which applicant groups need telephone or translated support?

tasks.short: Recommend candidates to managers using clear evidence and a consistent selection process.

today.trigger: Screened candidates and interview feedback are ready for a selection discussion.
steps: Review applications, screening notes and interview feedback.
Compare evidence against agreed job requirements.
Resolve conflicting feedback or missing evidence with interviewers and applicants.
Recommend candidates to the manager and record the decision.
drudgery: Chasing missing evaluation forms
Reformatting interview notes
Reconstructing why interviewers disagree
today.time_sinks: Feedback arrives late or uses vague judgements, leaving the recruiter to assemble a defensible recommendation.

lenses.faster: Prepare a source-linked comparison of completed evaluations and highlight unanswered questions. Feedback chasing follows fixed reminders.
lenses.autonomous: Request evaluations after interviews and flag incomplete submissions. Candidate recommendations and decisions remain with people.
lenses.ambitious: Provide a documented selection discussion for every hire, including high-volume warehouse hiring during peak season.
lenses.joy: Spend more time discussing evidence and helping managers make good decisions, with less time assembling notes.
lenses.options: Show candidates against each approved criterion and identify what an additional conversation or work sample could resolve.
lenses.altitude: Coach managers in evidence-based selection and improve the consistency of the decision process.
reach: Support HR Business Partners with interviewer coaching.
Help People Analytics examine selection quality and later onboarding outcomes.

tasks.human_edge: Weighing conflicting evidence, challenging manager assumptions and taking responsibility for a fair recommendation.
tasks.pattern_why: A copilot prepares evidence summaries and discussion questions while the recruiter leads comparison and recommendation. Fixed workflow rules handle reminders; no automated ranking determines who reaches a manager.

in_practice.trigger: The recruiter starts a selection review once the relevant interview stage is complete.
steps: Request outstanding structured evaluations through Recruitee and show their completion status.
Summarise submitted evidence by approved criterion, linking each statement to its source.
Flag disagreement, unsupported assertions and missing evidence without filling gaps.
Have the recruiter inspect the sources and write the recommendation for the manager.
Record the manager's decision and reasons before any candidate status communication is triggered.
in_practice.human_gate: The recruiter owns the recommendation; the authorised manager owns the hiring decision. Both can challenge the summary and inspect all original evidence.
data_needed: Approved job criteria
Verified screening findings
Structured interview evaluations
Relevant work-sample results
Decision authority and documented reasons
in_practice.logs_to: Recruitee stores evaluations, recruiter recommendation, manager decision and source references, with restricted access and applicant retention controls.

evidence.claim: Recruitee supports structured evaluation forms, scorecards and evaluation requests; these support consistent evidence collection.
Source-linked summaries could reduce preparation effort; 35% effort saved and 1.3 times faster turnaround are estimates, with manager availability still limiting elapsed time.

risks: A polished summary can make weak evidence look authoritative; require source checks and prohibit invented suitability or personality judgements.
Human approval can become a rubber stamp. Reviewers need time, authority and access to the original evidence.

Solely automated decisions with significant effects are restricted under AVG Article 22; this design keeps meaningful human selection. [GDPR Article 22](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng)
Human involvement does not itself remove a selection tool from the AI Act's high-risk category; include this use in the classification assessment.
research_questions: Do summaries preserve material disagreements and minority interviewer views?
How much of the current task is preparation rather than conversation and judgement?
Can managers use the same observable criteria across the three sites?
Does a pilot reduce review time while maintaining decision quality and candidate fairness?

tasks.short: Keep applicants informed about progress, delays and decisions.

today.trigger: An application changes stage, a decision is made or an applicant requests an update.
steps: Check the current application stage and the latest manager decision.
Find the applicant's last message and promised response date.
Write or adapt a status update and send it.
Record the contact and chase the next owner when the process is delayed.
drudgery: Sending repeated acknowledgement and progress messages
Checking who has not received an update
Maintaining personal follow-up reminders
today.time_sinks: Outdated stages and missing manager decisions force manual investigation before an accurate message can be sent.

lenses.faster: Use approved stage-specific messages and automatic overdue checks. Routine drafting and reminder tracking disappear.
lenses.autonomous: Send acknowledgements, confirmed progress updates and delay notices from recorded events; flag bounced messages and replies for follow-up.
lenses.ambitious: Give every applicant a reliable update cadence, including during seasonal hiring peaks.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive chasing while preserving personal feedback and difficult conversations.
lenses.options: Maintain short and detailed messages for different stages and applicant language needs, all grounded in the same recorded status.
lenses.altitude: Manage the reliability of candidate communication through overdue cases, delivery failures and complaint patterns.
reach: Help HR Administration design event-based employee updates.
Help People Analytics monitor communication delays by site and hiring manager.

tasks.human_edge: Giving thoughtful rejection feedback, repairing trust after delays and recognising when a call is needed.
tasks.pattern_why: The trigger, recorded status and approved message can be written as rules. Deterministic_software is sufficient; a model should not invent decisions, explanations or promised dates.

in_practice.trigger: An application event, approved decision or overdue-status check occurs in Recruitee.
steps: Confirm the latest application stage and whether the underlying decision has been approved.
Select the approved message and populate only verified fields.
Check previous sends and pending replies to prevent duplicate or contradictory messages.
Send the update and create a recruiter task for delivery failures, replies or unresolved delays.
Report overdue cases and pause affected automations when stage data is unreliable.
in_practice.human_gate: People make rejection, referral and offer decisions before messages are released. The recruiter personally approves sensitive feedback and handles disputes or unusual cases.
data_needed: Current application stage and approved decision
Last contact and promised update date
Approved message templates
Applicant contact details and language preference
Responsible recruiter and manager
in_practice.logs_to: Recruitee message and activity history, plus a restricted exception log for failed, suppressed and duplicate sends.

evidence.claim: Recruitee documents stage-based email and task automations.
Recruitee can send or schedule emails after a user disqualifies a candidate with a configured reason.
75% effort saved and 3 times faster turnaround are planning estimates; clean stage data and a high routine-message share are necessary.

risks: A wrong stage or recipient can send an inappropriate rejection or expose application information.
Re-entering a stage or retrying a failed event can generate duplicate messages unless previous sends are checked.
A holding message must not promise an interview, offer or date that has not been approved.
Automated messages can conceal manager delays; overdue ownership needs a named person.
research_questions: What proportion of current status contacts are routine enough for approved templates?
Are application stages updated accurately and promptly at every site?
Does the current Recruitee plan support the required triggers, conditions and scheduling?
Can a pilot meet update commitments without duplicate messages or increased complaints?

tasks.short: Find suitable candidates through talent pools, referrals, agencies and local recruitment channels.

today.trigger: A vacancy opens, an existing search stalls or seasonal demand increases.
steps: Clarify the role, site, shifts and likely candidate groups with the manager.
Search Recruitee records, referrals and permitted external recruitment sources.
Coordinate candidate supply with staffing agencies and local recruitment contacts.
Contact prospects and record responses, source and next steps.
drudgery: Rewriting search terms and outreach drafts
Finding duplicate candidate records
Rechecking whether older talent-pool records can still be used
today.time_sinks: Fragmented sources, outdated availability and unclear agency ownership create repeated searches and coordination.

lenses.faster: Generate search queries, check permitted talent-pool records and draft relevant outreach from the approved role brief.
lenses.autonomous: Run scheduled searches on authorised internal records and alert the recruiter to new evidence matches. External contact remains approved by the recruiter.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain useful candidate pools for recurring site and shift needs before vacancies become urgent, rather than repeatedly starting from scratch.
lenses.joy: Reduce repetitive searching and record cleaning so more time goes to referrals, community contacts and candidate relationships.
lenses.options: Compare internal mobility, referrals, local campaigns and agency supply as separate sourcing routes with their costs and likely lead times.
lenses.altitude: Design a sourcing mix based on productive, retained hires rather than application volume.
reach: Support HR Business Partners with internal mobility campaigns.
Prepare agency sourcing briefs and channel cost comparisons with Operations and Finance.

tasks.human_edge: Building trusted networks, understanding local labour markets and persuading someone to consider a realistic opportunity.
tasks.pattern_why: A copilot prepares searches, evidence lists and outreach drafts while the recruiter chooses sources and contacts. Deterministic checks handle duplicates and retention eligibility; unrestricted web scraping or autonomous mass outreach is unnecessary.

in_practice.trigger: An approved vacancy opens or the recruiter schedules a recurring sourcing review.
steps: Load the role brief, permitted sources and current recruitment priorities.
Generate search variants and search eligible Recruitee records using explicit job-related fields.
Present potential candidates with source evidence, record age and contact eligibility; flag possible duplicates.
Prepare outreach drafts and agency briefs for recruiter review, including any conversion restrictions requiring a contract check.
Record approved contacts, responses and source attribution for later outcome analysis.
in_practice.human_gate: The recruiter approves each new outreach recipient or reviewed campaign list and resolves agency ownership, privacy and contractual questions before contact.
data_needed: Approved role and shift requirements
Eligible talent-pool records and retention status
Referral information and source provenance
Agency terms and candidate ownership records
Recruitment source costs and mature 90-day outcomes
in_practice.logs_to: Recruitee records source provenance, contact basis, approved outreach and responses; aggregate channel outcomes feed a restricted Power BI report.

evidence.claim: Recruitee supports organising talent pools with tags, source tags and filters.
Search and outreach drafting assistance is plausible; 40% effort saved and 1.5 times faster turnaround are estimates, with relationship work remaining human.

risks: Publicly visible profiles are not unrestricted recruitment data; establish an appropriate basis, provide required information and respect source terms.

Reusing unsuccessful applicants requires retention eligibility. AP guidance describes deletion normally within four weeks, or longer retention with permission, with up to one year considered reasonable. [AP applicant-data guidance](https://autoriteitpersoonsgegevens.nl/themas/werk-en-uitkering/sollicitaties/persoonsgegevens-van-sollicitanten)
Agency ownership and conversion terms may affect approaching existing flex workers; check contracts before outreach.
Optimising only for familiar sources can repeatedly exclude candidates who use different channels.
research_questions: How many existing talent-pool records are current, contactable and eligible for reuse?
Which sources produce productive hires who remain after 90 days, once role, site and season are considered?
Do agency agreements permit the proposed sourcing and conversion routes?
Can query assistance improve useful candidate conversations per recruiter hour without narrowing access?

tasks.short: Check whether selection criteria are relevant, consistent and supported by evidence.

today.trigger: A selection process is introduced, complaints arise or hiring outcomes suggest that criteria need review.
steps: Gather vacancy criteria, interview questions, evaluation forms and available outcomes.
Compare criteria with actual job tasks and professional guidance.
Review consistency, missing evidence and potentially unfair requirements with specialists.
Recommend changes and obtain approval before updating the process.
drudgery: Comparing many slightly different versions of criteria
Cleaning inconsistent evaluation labels
Rebuilding the same review tables
today.time_sinks: Small samples, inconsistent job definitions and incomplete outcome links make reliable evaluation harder than producing a dashboard.

lenses.faster: Use code to compare criterion versions, find missing evaluations and calculate agreed descriptive measures. AI drafts a review note from the checked results.
lenses.autonomous: Schedule data-quality and criterion-change checks, with alerts for review rather than automatic changes to selection rules.
lenses.ambitious: Review recurring high-volume roles systematically and test whether entry barriers are necessary or could be replaced by training.
lenses.joy: Remove spreadsheet assembly so the recruiter can challenge weak assumptions and improve fairness with managers.
lenses.options: Compare keeping, removing or replacing a criterion, showing evidence gaps and plausible operational consequences.
lenses.altitude: Own the review cycle for selection standards while specialists judge legal and statistical validity.
reach: Prepare recruitment analyses with the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst.
Support HR Business Partners in revising recruitment policy.

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether criteria reflect actual work, recognising weak evidence and deciding when specialist validation is necessary.
tasks.pattern_why: Deterministic_software performs reproducible checks and calculations; a copilot drafts interpretations and revision options. Statistical validity, discrimination risk and policy changes require qualified human review.

in_practice.trigger: A quarterly review date arrives or a material criterion change or complaint opens a review.
steps: Build a restricted analysis dataset linking criterion versions, selection stages and permitted mature outcomes.
Run version-controlled checks for missing data, inconsistent use, sample size and descriptive associations.
Draft findings that distinguish observed association from causation and identify uncertainty.
Review findings with People Analytics, the HR Business Partner and relevant legal or assessment specialists.
Approve revisions through the appropriate policy and OR process, then monitor the new version.
in_practice.human_gate: People Analytics checks methods; the HR policy owner approves changes. Obtain OR consent where the proposed recruitment or privacy arrangement falls under its statutory rights.
systems: Proposed analysis scripts and approved LLM service
data_needed: Versioned criteria and evidence of job relevance
Selection-stage and evaluation records
Permitted links to employment and agreed productivity outcomes
Site, job family, shift and cohort dates
Specialist-approved analysis and minimum reporting thresholds
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint stores analysis code versions, data definitions, findings, specialist reviews and policy approvals; Power BI receives aggregate results only.

evidence.claim: Recruitee's structured evaluation forms provide a practical basis for collecting comparable criterion-level evidence.
Reproducible analysis could reduce preparation work, but statistical usefulness depends on data quality and sample size; 40% effort saved and 1.4 times faster turnaround are estimates.

risks: Outcomes exist mainly for hired applicants, so they cannot establish that rejected applicants would have performed poorly.
Retention and productivity also reflect supervision, onboarding and shift conditions; correlations do not establish criterion validity.
Fairness analysis may require sensitive data; use specialist-approved lawful methods and never infer protected characteristics from names or photographs.

Changes to recruitment policy or employee privacy arrangements can require OR consent. [SER guidance on consent rights](https://www.ser.nl/nl/thema/medezeggenschap/aan-de-slag-met-de-or/rechten/instemmingsrecht)
research_questions: Are there enough comparable hires and complete evaluations to support conclusions beyond descriptive findings?
Can Recruitee and AFAS records be linked reliably for an approved purpose without exposing unnecessary personal data?
Which criteria have documented job relevance or external validation, and which are inherited preferences?
Will specialist review and the OR process leave a worthwhile reduction in total review time?

tasks.short: Plan recruiting across sites so staffing needs become productive, retained hires.

today.trigger: Operations updates staffing needs, seasonal demand approaches or vacancies remain unfilled.
steps: Gather approved staffing needs, vacancies, recruitment results and agency supply information.
Discuss site and shift constraints with managers and HR Business Partners.
Choose channels, campaign timing and recruiter priorities within the approved budget.
Review results and change the plan when demand or hiring performance changes.
drudgery: Reconciling vacancy counts across spreadsheets and systems
Rebuilding campaign and funnel reports
Collecting the same planning inputs from three sites
today.time_sinks: Operations demand, agency supply and recruitment outcomes use different definitions and update cycles.

lenses.faster: Create a checked planning pack from vacancies, approved staffing demand and recruitment outcomes. Scenario calculations replace repeated spreadsheet rebuilding.
lenses.autonomous: Refresh the pack after the nightly AFAS extract and alert the recruiter when agreed vacancy or funnel thresholds are crossed.
lenses.ambitious: Plan backwards from the date a site needs productive staff, including selection lead time, week-one onboarding and required training capacity.
lenses.joy: Move time from reconciling reports to solving site-specific recruitment problems with Operations.
lenses.options: Compare earlier campaigns, different channel mixes, internal moves, flex-to-permanent routes and additional onboarding capacity under explicit assumptions.
lenses.altitude: Become the designer of recruitment capacity and feedback loops across all three sites.
reach: Draft workforce supply scenarios with HR Business Partners and Operations.
Prepare recruitment budget and agency-cost inputs for FP&A and the Controller.

tasks.human_edge: Choosing trade-offs under uncertain demand, securing manager commitment and knowing when a recruitment problem is really a pay, shift or onboarding problem.
tasks.pattern_why: Deterministic calculations produce transparent scenarios and a copilot drafts options. People choose priorities, spending and operational commitments because the inputs and trade-offs remain uncertain.

in_practice.trigger: A weekly planning cycle follows the nightly AFAS refresh, or Operations submits a material demand change.
steps: Combine approved demand and vacancy data with recruitment funnel measures, agency capacity and onboarding constraints.
Reconcile definitions and show source timestamps, missing inputs and unmatched records.
Calculate scenarios using explicit conversion rates, lead times, costs and training capacity assumptions.
Draft recruitment priorities and identify which bottlenecks need action from Operations, HR or Learning and Development.
Have the recruiter and HR Business Partners agree the plan with Operations and obtain required budget approval before execution.
in_practice.human_gate: Operations owns staffing demand, HR leadership owns recruitment priorities and authorised budget holders approve spending; the recruiter recommends and coordinates.
systems: Studytube enrolment and completion extracts where available
data_needed: Approved headcount and staffing demand by role, site, shift and date
Openings, application stages, offer acceptance and hiring lead times
Agency capacity and agreed commercial terms
Week-one onboarding and relevant training capacity
Mature 90-day retention and manager-confirmed productivity outcomes
Approved budgets and channel costs
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint stores dated scenarios, assumptions, decisions and owners; Power BI tracks agreed measures with visible refresh dates.

evidence.claim: AFAS provides GetConnectors for retrieving selected Profit data; an appropriately authorised extract is technically possible, but the required dataset must be configured.
Combining approved demand, recruitment and onboarding inputs into transparent scenarios is plausible; 35% effort saved and 1.3 times faster turnaround are estimates.

risks: Nightly AFAS data is unsuitable as live shift availability; show timestamps and obtain current operational confirmation.
Seasonal changes can invalidate historical conversion rates and agency availability.
Early cohorts have not reached day 90; report them as pending rather than treating them as successes or failures.
Recruiters should not receive individual absence histories or medical data for planning. Wet verbetering poortwachter case management remains with the responsible absence team.
research_questions: Does Operations provide approved staffing demand early enough to change recruitment timing?
Can each site define productive consistently, and who records that outcome?
Can training and onboarding capacity be measured before campaigns increase applicant supply?
Do scenario-led decisions improve the share of openings producing a productive, retained 90-day hire?

tasks.short: Organise job-relevant applicant tests and check whether they support fair selection.

today.trigger: A role needs an assessment, a candidate reaches the assessment stage or an existing test needs review.
steps: Agree what the assessment should measure and consult a qualified specialist where needed.
Choose or develop job-related tasks and scoring guidance.
Arrange invitations, assessors, facilities and any requested adjustments.
Collect results and review their interpretation and usefulness with the hiring team.
drudgery: Sending invitations and reminders
Preparing repeated assessment instructions
Collecting assessor forms and compiling results
today.time_sinks: Assessment logistics, inconsistent scoring and specialist approval consume time; valid test development cannot be reduced to generating questions.

lenses.faster: Draft instructions and scoring rubrics, automate scheduling reminders and assemble completed assessor forms.
lenses.autonomous: Trigger approved assessment invitations and completion reminders from the pipeline. Results requiring judgement stay with trained assessors.
lenses.ambitious: Use well-designed work samples for recurring roles, such as checking a pick list or handling a customer exception, rather than relying only on CV presentation.
lenses.joy: Remove assessment administration so the recruiter can improve relevance, accessibility and candidate experience with specialists.
lenses.options: Compare a structured interview, short work sample and existing validated assessment, including candidate burden and administration cost.
lenses.altitude: Manage the quality of the assessment process and its evidence rather than personally building and scoring every test.
reach: Coordinate safe work samples and assessor training with Learning and Development.
Help People Analytics review assessment completion, consistency and later outcomes.

tasks.human_edge: Judging job relevance, safeguarding accessibility and dignity, and recognising when qualified assessment or occupational-health expertise is required.
tasks.pattern_why: A copilot drafts assessment materials while deterministic_software handles administration. Test validity, psychological interpretation and practical safety remain with qualified people; generated questions are not validated tests.

in_practice.trigger: A recruiter requests an assessment design review or a candidate reaches an approved assessment stage.
steps: Choose the approved assessment and document the job criterion it measures.
Use AI only to draft or adapt permitted instructions and work-sample materials for specialist review.
Obtain approval of scoring, accessibility, safety and candidate information before release.
Send invitations and reminders, then collect human assessor results in restricted structured forms.
Have qualified reviewers interpret results and periodically assess consistency and usefulness before changing the test.
in_practice.human_gate: A qualified specialist approves assessment design and interpretation; trained assessors judge practical work. The recruiter and hiring manager retain the selection decision.
systems: Approved LLM service for drafting, proposed
data_needed: Job-task analysis and approved assessment purpose
Permitted test materials, provider terms and validation evidence
Scoring rubrics and assessor qualifications
Adjustment arrangements with restricted handling of sensitive information
Completion records, assessor results and permitted outcome data
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint assessment register stores versions and approvals; Recruitee stores necessary results and decision reasons, without duplicating raw psychological or medical records.

evidence.claim: Recruitee supports scheduling candidate events and requesting structured evaluations from interviewers or assessors.
Drafting and administration assistance is plausible, but it does not validate a test; 35% effort saved and 1.2 times faster turnaround are estimates.

risks: Generated tests can measure language familiarity or test-taking skill instead of job capability; require appropriate validation and accessible alternatives.
Do not use facial, voice or emotion inference to judge candidates; it introduces unnecessary legal and validity risks.
Practical warehouse assessments need safe conditions and qualified supervision; completing a work sample does not award a forklift or other mandatory certificate.

Health questions and medical examinations have separate restrictions; use the proper occupational-health route rather than recruiter-designed medical screening. [AP health-data guidance](https://autoriteitpersoonsgegevens.nl/themas/werk-en-uitkering/sollicitaties/gegevens-over-gezondheid-bij-sollicitaties)
Automated assessment scores must not silently determine progression; assess AVG Article 22 and the intended AI Act use before introduction.
research_questions: Which roles need an assessment, and what evidence shows that it measures an essential job capability?
Is a qualified provider or specialist available to approve validity, scoring and adjustments?
Can administrative effort fall without increasing candidate burden or reducing accessibility?
Are sample sizes sufficient to review assessor consistency and useful links to later performance?

role.altitude: The recruiter becomes the owner of a reliable recruitment process: clear requirements, accurate candidate information, evidence-based selection and feedback from onboarding through day 90. Routine administration runs through checked workflows; the recruiter spends more time with candidates and managers.
reach: Prepare workforce supply scenarios with HR Business Partners and Operations.
Coordinate the recruitment-to-onboarding hand-off with HR Administration and Learning and Development.
Prepare recruitment channel and agency-cost analyses for Finance.
Coach hiring managers on structured interviews and documented selection.
Maintain recruitment process definitions and data-quality checks with the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst.
role.ceiling_note: Current workflows are inferred from the supplied company context, not observed. These eight tasks total 1,107.4 hours per FTE annually, about 69.2% of the stated role. The proposed effort savings imply roughly 1,075 hours across both recruiters, worth about EUR 69,900 annually at EUR 65/hour before implementation, licences, maintenance and overlap. This is potential capacity, not a cash saving or headcount recommendation; the remaining role time is unassessed. Task speedups estimate elapsed turnaround including routine processing and review, so they are lower than effort reductions where waiting remains. Manager availability, qualified assessment expertise, candidate trust and onboarding capacity limit further gains. Use the company's actual systems; the O*NET software list does not establish that Workday, Oracle or Kronos is installed.
skills_to_grow: Write observable job criteria and distinguish essential requirements from trainable skills.
Check AI summaries against original evidence and recognise automation bias.
Configure and monitor recruitment workflows, templates and exception queues.
Understand recruitment data protection, meaningful human review and applicable EU AI Act duties.
Work with HR leadership on OR involvement when recruitment or privacy arrangements change.
Interpret funnel measures, mature cohorts and uncertain outcome comparisons.
Design realistic job previews and coach structured interviews.
